scope.description: Measure how much caller-supplied payload the leader retains when many distinct ReadIndex requests are accepted while it cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements, and verify that each retained payload is a distinct buffer rather than one shared slice counted repeatedly.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); no MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, so every read takes the queued path.

64 requests are submitted, each carrying its own freshly allocated 4096-byte RequestCtx, modelling a caller issuing distinct reads (the ReadIndex API takes an opaque rctx []byte and documents no size limit).

Retention is summed over the Data fields of the entries held in pendingReadIndexMessages, and the number of distinct backing buffers is counted by taking the address of each buffer's first byte, so a shared slice would appear as distinct_ctx_buffers < pending.
excluded: Any claim about total process footprint (allocator overhead, per-message structs and slice headers are not counted) or about a specific deployment's memory limit.
Any claim that a caller must not send large contexts; only that the library accepts and retains whatever it is given.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexRetainedBytes builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, clears the outbound buffers, and emits a setup event with CheckQuorum, state, voter count, the per-request context size and the round count. It then submits 64 MsgReadIndex messages, each with its own 4096-byte Data buffer, clearing outbound traffic each round, and finally emits a probe event with the pending queue length, the summed retained Data length, the number of distinct backing buffers and the node state.

comparisons.description: Every one of the 64 distinct read requests is retained.
The retained caller payload is 64 times 4096 bytes, i.e. the retry count multiplied by the caller-chosen context size.
The byte total is genuine retention: the 64 payloads sit in 64 distinct buffers, so the sum is not one shared slice counted repeatedly.

knowledge.assertion: the queued path retains one message per request and is not reclaimed
